solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Final couples in twist are dancing with vigour

indicators.note: the final couple in each word means its closing two letters, taken in turn from the four words that follow

explanation.surface: Twisting couples hit the dance floor with plenty of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final couples in' takes the last two letters of twist, are, dancing and with: ST, RE, NG, TH. 'with' looks like a link word but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigour and strength both mean physical power or force, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Rare shock when Conservative gets in

indicators.note: the Conservative abbreviation gets inside the word for a shock, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a shock is a scare

explanation.surface: An unusual upset at an election when the Conservative candidate wins.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is in short supply, the usual synonym for scarce.

clue.text: Greek island with extremely rich poetry

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters of the next word are used

parts.note: odes are poems, so poetry gives ODES

explanation.surface: A Greek island blessed with lavish verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a large island in the Dodecanese, belonging to Greece.

clue.text: Vague idea of a negative particle

parts.note: not is a negative word
an ion is a charged particle

explanation.surface: A hazy concept about a negatively charged particle in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: A notion is a vague belief or impression, a loose idea rather than a firm one.

clue.text: Test hothead ruined, losing seconds — fatally!

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the two words before it are wrecked and rebuilt in another order
losing says a letter must be dropped from the reworked letters

explanation.surface: A hot-headed cricketer wrecks a Test match and loses it in seconds, with fatal results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing seconds' drops one S from TEST HOTHEAD; 'ruined' rearranges the ten letters left into the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting to the death means until one side dies, so the phrase means fatally.

clue.text: Little bird is found inside hide!

indicators.note: found inside says one word sits within another

parts.note: a hide is an animal's skin

explanation.surface: A small bird is spotted hiding in a birdwatcher's hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hide' suggests a birdwatching shelter, which fits the little bird, but here it means an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The siskin is a small European finch, a little songbird.

clue.text: Presswoman at No 10, once?

parts.note: a woman who presses clothes uses an iron, and the nickname given to Margaret Thatcher, the former Prime Minister living at No 10 Downing Street, fits that whimsical picture

explanation.surface: A former press secretary working at Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presswoman' suggests a journalist, but split it as press (iron) plus woman (lady). No 10 Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's residence; Margaret Thatcher was its famous female occupant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Lady was the nickname of Margaret Thatcher, Britain's Prime Minister from 1979 to 1990.

clue.text: Support aim to stop strikes, essentially

parts.note: to keep someone is to support them financially
a goal is an aim

explanation.surface: Backing the bid to prevent industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' suggests walkouts, but here it means shots at goal.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep goal is to act as goalkeeper, whose essential job is stopping shots.

clue.text: Stuff may be associated with this rubbish

definitions.text: Stuff may be associated with this
definitions.meaning: the stock phrase stuff and ... dismisses something as foolish talk

explanation.walkthrough: The British exclamation 'stuff and nonsense!' means 'rubbish!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonsense is foolish talk, the same thing as rubbish in its spoken sense.

clue.text: Deserter gets a job making tea

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: making suggests the letters of the next word are made into something new

explanation.surface: A runaway soldier finds work as a tea-maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate abandons their faith or cause, so is a deserter of it.

clue.text: With it the navy follows procedure

indicators.note: follows puts the navy abbreviation after the word for procedure

parts.note: a mode is a way of doing things, a procedure
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: In this matter, the navy sticks to protocol.
explanation.definitionFit: Being with it means being fashionable and up to date, which is modern.

clue.text: Cut in insurance to think about

indicators.note: in places the word for cut inside the word for insurance

parts.note: insurance is cover
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A cut in insurance benefits, something to ponder.
explanation.definitionFit: To chew something over is an idiom for mulling it over or considering it at length.

clue.text: Silver in colour, like 8

indicators.note: in puts the symbol for silver within the colour

parts.note: blue is a colour
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A silver thread woven into a coloured fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 refers to the answer to 8 Down, meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Blague is a rare word, from French, for humbug or empty talk, matching the cross-referenced rubbish.

clue.text: Doctor recalled in rags-to-riches tale

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next two words are altered

explanation.surface: A physician is called back to take part in a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun but is a verb: it rearranges RECALLED IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella is the fairy tale of a mistreated girl in rags who marries a prince.

clue.text: Where alcohol is kept locked up

definitions.meaning: drinks are stored behind the bar of a pub
locked up means imprisoned, held in a cell

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the phrase literally: behind the counters of pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Behind bars is an idiom for in prison, and literally where a pub keeps its drink.

clue.text: Possibly easiest one, in my opinion

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Perhaps the simplest one, I reckon.
explanation.definitionFit: As I see it is an idiom meaning from my point of view.

clue.text: Arrange to show time, not key, like this musician

indicators.note: to show time means the time letter is put on display in the arranged word
not key means the key letter is the one that is removed and replaced

parts.note: to organise is to arrange
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A conductor arranges the piece to change its tempo and key.
explanation.definitionFit: An organist is a musician who plays the organ.

clue.text: Still popular stage show I've taken on

indicators.note: taken on means added on at the end

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an act is a stage turn or show

explanation.surface: A popular stage show that I've signed up for.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means motionless, and inactive means not moving or doing anything.

clue.text: High water content of sprout diet, perhaps

parts.note: to sprout is to spring up

indicators.note: perhaps says the word before it is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: The water content of a diet of sprouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content of' is a link; 'perhaps' rearranges DIET into TIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring tide is the especially high tide at new and full moon.

clue.text: Repeat call before admitting sergeant

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a sergeant is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A call made ahead of letting the sergeant in.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience cries encore to call for a repeat performance.

clue.text: Substitute not quite satisfying hunger

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls a letter short of complete

parts.note: a filling meal satisfies hunger

explanation.surface: A replacement meal that doesn't quite fill you up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fill-in is a stand-in or temporary replacement for someone.

clue.text: Slides or photographs, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to shoot a subject is to photograph it

explanation.surface: Choosing between slides and prints in a photo show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slides' suggests photographic transparencies, but means playground slides.
explanation.definitionFit: Chutes are sloping channels down which things or people slide.

clue.text: Pakistan certainly takes this position when batting

indicators.note: takes means the phrase holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Pakistan's batsmen surely adopt this stance at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A batter's stance is how they stand at the crease in cricket or baseball.

clue.text: Wave around one's breakfast bowl?

parts.note: bran is a breakfast cereal
a dish is a bowl

explanation.surface: Waving your cereal bowl about over breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to wave something, typically a weapon, about.

clue.text: Extract not allowed on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as heard spoken on air

parts.note: illicit means not allowed, unlawful

explanation.surface: Banned extracts broadcast on air.
explanation.definitionFit: To elicit is to draw out or extract a response or information.

clue.text: Like a match held in the dark, no doubt

definitions.text: Like a match held in the dark, no doubt

parts.words: Like a match held in the dark, no doubt
parts.note: a lit match held in darkness seems the picture, but the match is a sports fixture played at night under bright lights

explanation.walkthrough: 'match' suggests a lit matchstick; it is a football game played after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: A night fixture is lit by floodlights, so it is a lit-up sporting event.

clue.text: Three central locations could give you the lead

indicators.note: central means the middle letter of the word that follows
could give you suggests the letters may be rearranged to yield something else

explanation.surface: Three central sites might put you in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central' takes T, the middle letter of 'locations'; 'could give you' rearranges THREE plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: A tether is a rope or lead tying an animal to something.

clue.text: Processions take a long time in 8

indicators.note: take means hold inside, so the long time goes within the cross-referenced word

parts.note: 8 refers to 8 Down, meaning rubbish; pants is British slang for rubbish
an age is a long time

explanation.surface: Parades that go on forever in a load of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang meaning rubbish or worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Pageants are elaborate public shows, often parades or processions.
